text: In the Scholium to the Principia, Newton characterizes absolute, true, and mathematical time as time that:
choices: Is merely the order of succession among non-simultaneous events
Cannot be conceived at all apart from the succession of ideas in the mind
In itself, and of its own nature, flows equably (uniformly) without relation to anything external
Is the form of inner sense, empirically real yet transcendentally ideal
explanation: Newton's Scholium defines absolute time as flowing 'equably... without relation to anything external' — an independent framework that would pass even in a universe with no events, matter, or change. Choice 0 is Leibniz's relationalism, choice 1 is the empiricist (Locke/Berkeley) view that our idea of time derives from mental succession, and choice 3 is Kant's transcendental account; all are positions that Newton's absolutism opposed.
